## 15. Conventions and gotchas

- **Never silently swallow exceptions.** Don't write `except Exception: pass`.
  Use `core.safe.swallow(...)` / `swallowed(...)` (GUI side) or
  `aw_safe.swallow(...)` / `swallowed(...)` (pipeline / `services` / `widgets`,
  none of which may import `review`) so a suppressed failure still leaves a
  DEBUG breadcrumb. Enforced by `tests/test_no_silent_except.py`, which names
  `review/`, `widgets/`, `datasets/` and the pipeline modules one area at a
  time — each with the helper that area may use — and then runs the rule over
  **everything `tests/_repo_scan.py` calls application code**, root modules and
  `scripts/` included. The area tests were the whole surface until that last one
  landed, and between them they left exactly the files the remaining handlers
  were in. (Two near-identical helpers exist on purpose: the pipeline must not
  import `review` — see §6.2.) The handful of sites where swallowing is
  correct are allowlisted by *file and function*, never by file, so an exemption
  cannot cover the next handler added beside it; a liveness test fails when an
  entry stops naming a real handler. Those sites are the crash reporter in
  `startup/boot_diag.py` — where an escaping exception loses the crash report, the one
  artifact that makes a native crash diagnosable — matplotlib's font-cache
  rebuild, and `remote_bootstrap._quietly`'s own last-resort note to stderr.
- **Never hardcode colours.** Use `ui.theme.Colors.*` or QSS object names.
- **Never block the UI thread.** Heavy operations spawn workers (see
  `review/features/smfish/worker.py` and the `services.pipeline_runner`
  pattern). Streaming progress messages route through `logging` and the
  status-bar label.
- **Plate selections are well IDs (strings), not (row, col) tuples.**
  `_selected_wells: set[str]`. Convert to / from tuples at the
  edge with `data_loading.parse_well_token`.
- **Parse a well name with `util.well_token`, never a local regex.** The
  canonicaliser strips surrounding whitespace, uppercases the row and
  zero-pads the column (`" a1 "` → `"A01"`), and returns `None` for anything
  outside A–H / 1–12. Ask it once and use what it returns rather than
  validating and then re-matching — `canonical_well_label` is both the test and
  the conversion. A second parser is not a style problem: when the pipeline
  carried its own, a folder named `"A1 "` was a well to the Analyze-side input
  resolver and not a well to the pipeline that then processed it. A local copy
  drifts in both directions at once — the ones this rule displaced rejected a
  trailing space and a lower-case `a1/` directory that the canonicaliser
  accepts, while accepting an `A0` or `A13` that it rejects.
  **A digit means an ASCII digit.** `\d` is Unicode by default and matches some
  six hundred decimal digits, and `int()` / `float()` convert all of them, so
  `"A1"`, `"A１"` and `"A١"` — three distinct filename tokens naming three
  distinct files — all canonicalised to `"A01"` and merged onto one well.
  `util/well_token` and `util/timepoint` — the two modules whose parse decides
  *identity*, and where a merge is therefore unrecoverable — spell their digit
  classes `[0-9]`, and `parse_hours` gates its bare-`float()` fallback on `str.isascii`
  because the regex is not the only way a number gets out of that function. A
  token whose digits come from another alphabet is opaque, and an opaque token is
  kept as-is rather than guessed at — which is what both modules already promise
  everywhere else. `util/fov` and `util/schema_infer` still spell theirs `\d`,
  deliberately: nothing there decides identity. `parse_fov`'s own docstring
  records the reason — only *sorting* depends on it, equality still compares the
  raw token strings, and `sort_key`'s last tuple element is that raw token — so
  a non-ASCII digit costs an ordering, never a merge.
  `tests/test_well_token_single_parser.py` fails on any *whole-token* well
  pattern outside `util/well_token.py`. Two neighbouring shapes are deliberately
  not caught by it, because they are different operations: a **trailing**-token
  extractor reading a well off the end of a longer stem
  (`domain/viewer_state.extract_well_token`, `datasets/core/dataset_paths.split_stem_well`),
  and a **filename-shape** matcher (`<WELL>_out.zip` in
  `data/image_discovery.py`) — which still hands the token it captures to the
  canonicaliser rather than padding it itself. Log-line scrapers in `services/`
  are the third: they recover a well from a message the pipeline already
  formatted.
- **Normalise FOV / timepoint tokens with
  `data.image_resolver.normalize_numeric_token`.** These arrive from filenames,
  CSV columns and combo text, so `1`, `01` and `1.0` must collapse to one key
  before anything compares them. A local copy that formats differently strands
  a filter silently — a combo whose text never matches any row.
- **Read a timepoint token as hours with `util.timepoint.parse_hours`, and sort
  timepoints with `util.timepoint.sort_key`.** Both are stdlib-only, so the
  pipeline, `services/` and `review/` all import them (`services/` may not
  import `review` — §6.2 — which is what forced a separate copy before).
  Three names remain for call-site reasons and all delegate:
  `domain.image_identity.parse_timepoint_hours` (the viewer's, consumed by
  `normalize_tp` for canonical keys), `pipeline.auto_threshold.parse_tp_hours`,
  and `process_microscopy._parse_timepoint_hours` — the last a deliberate
  `nan`-returning adapter, so `timepoint_hours` stays a float column with no
  `None` to special-case into the CSV. Its one trade is that a literal `"nan"`
  token and an unreadable one are indistinguishable in its return; use
  `parse_hours` and test for `None` when that matters.
  `tests/test_timepoint_parsing.py` fuzzes the parsers against each other and
  asserts the sort-key identity, so a reintroduced local copy fails there. The
  grammar is deliberately strict: it will not scavenge a digit from anywhere in
  the token, because a guessed number becomes a canonical key nothing else
  recognises.
  **Emptiness is decided on `None`, never on the value's truthiness.** Both
  `parse_hours` and `sort_key` stringify through `util.timepoint._token`, the
  stdlib-only twin of `domain.image_identity._raw_token`, for the reason that rule
  exists at all: a numeric `0` is falsy, and `0` is the timepoint every time
  course starts at. Under `str(value or "")` a baseline arriving as a number
  rather than as text read as no token at all, which each consumer then
  expressed in its own vocabulary — `parse_hours` answered "unreadable",
  `sort_key`'s `(unparseable, …)` tuple put it *after* the twelve-hour column
  with the opaque labels, and `process_microscopy._parse_timepoint_hours`
  returned the `nan` its `h != h` callers read as raw-passthrough. The
  duplicated helper is the cost of this module's stdlib-only contract; both
  copies say so.
- **A confirmation that could not be obtained is not consent.** A destructive
  action guarded by a dialog has to return when the dialog *raises*, not fall
  through to the destructive call. Offscreen, `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse
  `_no_modal_dialogs` makes `QMessageBox.question` raise, which is exactly the
  dialog-unavailable case in the field, and `saved_plots/tab_view._confirm_clear`
  wiped the whole gallery through it. Wrap the *ask*, not the act: a suppressed
  failure around the question means "no answer", and the only safe reading of
  no answer is no.
- **Selections survive a tab switch.** Whenever you read or write
  `_selected_wells`, you're touching app-wide state — clobbering it in a
  tab-local handler will leak across tabs.
- **Don't call controllers' `redraw` directly from a widget signal.**
  Route through the shim on `ReviewApp`. The shim knows how to
  defer / batch / no-op when the relevant tab hasn't been built yet.
- **Lazy tab builds are real.** Don't assume `app._heatmap_fig` exists; do
  `if hasattr(app, "_heatmap_canvas"): …`.
- **Pipeline runs in a separate process.** Don't try to share Python
  objects between Analyze and the running pipeline; everything passes
  through argv → stdout text streaming → the dataset folder.
- **`_Docs/Markdowns/` is documentation, not code.** It is kept intentionally
  small: this file, the user README, and the teardown roadmap. The
  selections-model contract lives in its module docstring, not a separate doc.
  Port-time plans and status write-ups stay in git history.

If you read all the way to here and the structure still doesn't make sense,
the right next move is to open `review/runtime_app.py` and scroll
through `_build_ui` (around line 934) — that's where every widget tree
hanging off `ReviewApp` gets stitched together, and every name you'll
need to grep for is in plain sight.

---

## 16. Enforced contracts (guardrail tests)

Many of the rules above are not just prose — they're checked in CI by AST
guardrail tests, so contract drift fails the suite rather than rotting silently.
The map (each rule links to the test that holds it):

| Contract (§) | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| Pipeline self-sufficiency — no `review`/`widgets`/Qt anywhere under `pipeline/` or `util/`, nor in `process_microscopy.py` / `pipeline/well_plate_zipper.py`, at any nesting (§6.2). Scoped by directory walk rather than a file list, so a new module in either package is covered from the moment it exists | `tests/test_architecture_contracts.py::test_pipeline_is_self_sufficient` |
| Every repo-root module the pipeline imports is uploaded to the remote (§6.2) | `tests/test_remote_manifest.py` + `test_remote_runner.py::test_required_files_list_is_what_we_promised` |
| `services/` stay Qt-free (CLI-reusable, §13) | `test_architecture_contracts.py::test_services_have_no_qt_imports` |
| `widgets/` carry no app coupling (§13) | `test_architecture_contracts.py::test_widgets_do_not_import_the_app` |
| Every top-level package of application code is in `tests/_repo_scan.py`'s `PACKAGE_ROOTS`, and every entry there names a directory that exists. A package the roster omits is invisible to every AST guard at once, and the omission makes the suite *greener* — there is nothing else that measures a guard walking past code it was never handed | `tests/test_scan_surface_is_complete.py` |
| The repository root holds only entry points, repository configuration and packages (§3) — every root `.py` is in a roster with a written reason, and no roster entry names a file that has gone. A loose module imports exactly as well as a packaged one, so the entire cost of misplacement falls on whoever next goes looking for it, and nothing else would report it. The same test holds `_Docs/_Installation/build_all_well.sh`'s `REQUIRED` preflight roster against the tree — it required `analyze_tab.py` long after the Analyze pane became `analyze/tab.py`, and since the script exits 1 on the first missing entry, no release could be cut from it | `tests/test_root_holds_only_entry_points.py` |
| The PyInstaller spec's own **imports** resolve, not just the rosters it bundles. PyInstaller executes the spec as Python, and it imports first-party code at module scope — `scripts.profile_build`, `services.remote_runner`, `ui.theme` to validate a baked `ALLWELL_THEME`. A stale one is not a missing file in the bundle, it is a build that will not start, and the `ALLWELL_THEME` import sits inside a conditional so only a themed build reaches it: the default build stays green while the themed one is broken. Nothing in the suite executes the spec, so the first symptom is otherwise a release that cannot be built | `tests/test_spec_ships_every_first_party_module.py::test_the_spec_imports_only_modules_that_exist` |
| Every `--run-*` branch of `all_well_launcher._dispatch` imports a module that exists **and** calls that module's own `main()`. Both halves are needed: importing the zipper and then calling the pipeline's `main()` satisfies the import check while a frozen grouping run silently performs a pipeline run instead. Checked against the syntax tree, because `all_well_launcher` is the one module no test may import | `tests/test_zipper_frozen_dispatch.py` |
| `services.input_resolution_service.ZIPPER_SCRIPT` resolves to the `pipeline.well_plate_zipper` module itself. The grouping pre-pass is reached by **path** rather than by import, so nothing in Python notices when the path stops describing the tree: `find_zipper_script()` answers `None` and `run_zipper` raises only at the moment a user starts a run on a folder of loose TIFs. Identity rather than existence, because a constant pointing at `pipeline/__init__.py` would satisfy an `.exists()` check while spawning a subprocess that does nothing. The other rosters naming this file (`services.remote_manifest`, the build script's `REQUIRED` array, the spec's package walk) each read their own list against the tree and none of them reads this constant | `tests/test_zipper_script_path_resolves.py` |
| `core/` never imports a pane. The dependency runs one way — a pane reaches into this package, never the reverse — and a module here that needs `review/`, `analyze/` or `datasets/` is a pane's module that happens to sit in `core/`, which re-creates the tangle the package exists to remove (`analyze` importing `core` importing `review`) | `test_architecture_contracts.py::test_core_does_not_import_a_pane` |
| `core.profile._repo_root` and `startup.app_fonts.fonts_dir` resolve the repository root by counting parents from their own `__file__`, so each count is that module's address rather than a constant. A wrong count raises nothing: no profile resolves and every build falls back silently to the full application, or no bundled face registers and the application draws in a system font. Both are held against the repository root rather than re-derived from the module's own location, because a test that computes the answer the same way the module does accepts whatever the module says | `tests/test_profile_repo_root.py`, `tests/test_app_fonts_dir.py` |
| Controllers reach the app via the `app` arg, not by importing `ReviewApp` (§9) | `test_architecture_contracts.py::test_nothing_imports_reviewapp_at_runtime` |
| EventBus is a capped catalogue of exactly 5 signals (§9) | `test_architecture_contracts.py::test_event_bus_signal_catalogue_is_capped` |
| Feature-module naming scheme (§3) | `test_architecture_contracts.py::test_feature_module_naming` |
| One definition of "is this well complete" — no module outside `pipeline/completeness.py` spells out the dataset-health states as its own roster, so the states a plate legend paints cannot diverge from the states the classifier returns (§6.2, §6b) | `tests/test_no_second_completeness_predicate.py`, with its bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| One definition of what a run did to a well — no module outside `services/run_journal.py` spells out the run-journal well states as its own roster, so a state the runner records cannot be one a reader has never heard of and silently reports as something else (§6.5) | `tests/test_no_second_journal_vocabulary.py`, with its bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| Every analysis domain reaches the provenance log — each `ANALYSIS_SCOPES` storage domain has a stored location in `review/persistence/provenance.STORED_AT` or a written reason in `RECORDED_UNDER`, and neither names a domain that is not analysis state (§5.7) | `tests/test_review_provenance.py::test_every_analysis_domain_reaches_the_log`, with `::test_the_roster_guard_bites` |
| One definition of where a remote run lives — no module builds `{remote_staging_dir}/runs/{run_id}` from a literal outside `remote_run_dir` / `remote_run_paths`. It was spelled nine times across three classes while the dataset address beside it had one definition, and the half-sweeps that produced left a re-attaching run's own directory uncreated. | `tests/test_one_definition_of_the_run_dir.py`, with its bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py`. Matched on the literal's static text, so the spelling of the run-id expression cannot dodge it, and on the *position* of a bare `"runs"` segment for the two builders that never write a separator — `posixpath.join(staging, "runs", run_id)` and `PurePosixPath(staging) / "runs" / run_id`. Reading only f-strings left `%`, `.format` and `+` concatenation as ways around the rule. Scanned through `tests/_repo_scan.py` — the first version read one hardcoded file and went vacuous the moment an extraction moved code out of it — and it fails when it cannot find the funnel at all, rather than passing with nothing to compare against. |
| `domain/` & `data/` never import `features/` (the layering) | `tests/test_layering.py` |
| No silent broad-except anywhere (§15) — the four area tests, plus one over the whole `_repo_scan` surface (root modules and `scripts/` included) with a per-site, file-and-function allowlist and a liveness test | `tests/test_no_silent_except.py` |
| Nothing deletes a directory it only partly archived. Every path that turns a `<well>/` into `<well>.zip` packs an extension-filtered subset, so removing the folder destroyed the companion XML, acquisition logs and mask subdirectories the filter skipped. Archive-writing is followed one call deep within a module, because the two worst sites zipped through a one-line helper and a guard matching only a literal `atomic_zip` found two of the four (§6.5) | `tests/test_no_unarchived_delete.py`, with its bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| Every figure registered as `_*_fig` has a `_FIG_PREF_KEY_MAP` entry, so its axis and mark prefs key on a stable name rather than on `id(fig)` and survive a reload (§5.8) | `tests/test_figure_pref_keys.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| A function that returns a value on one path and an explicit `None` on another declares it. Without the annotation a caller cannot tell "no value" from "computed zero" by signature, which is the conflation behind this codebase's silently-wrong numbers | `tests/test_optional_returns_declared.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| No annotation reads a name nothing binds. Every module carries `from __future__ import annotations`, so an annotation is stored as a string and never compiled — invisible to `symtable` below (ruff's F821 is enforced, but an annotation string is not compiled, so it does not reach that rule either). An extraction dropped `Iterable` from a `collections.abc` import while the annotation needing it moved intact: nothing raised at import or at call, and `typing.get_type_hints` on that function raised `NameError`. A `TYPE_CHECKING` import counts as bound; a string forward reference is not this guard's to judge | `tests/test_no_unbound_names.py::test_no_annotation_reads_a_name_nothing_binds`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py`. The first cut allowlisted `dir(typing)`, which contains `Iterable`, `Callable`, `Mapping` and `Sequence` — the names a dropped import loses — so it passed on the defect it was written for |
| No function reads a name nothing binds. Ruff's F821 is enforced now and catches the plain cases, but the shape that gets past it is what a rename leaves behind — replace `a, b, c = thing()` with `obj = thing()` and every downstream `a` becomes a `NameError` no linter mentions, often on a path only the slow lane reaches | `tests/test_no_unbound_names.py` (`symtable`, so closures and comprehensions are not false positives), with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| The fold-change request is read by name, never unpacked | `tests/test_fc_state_is_not_unpacked.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| Every `ControlOutcome` is produced by a real collection and consumed by the editor, the status line and the CSV | `tests/test_control_outcome_roster.py` |
| `runtime_app` line/attr ratchets + state-package import boundary | `tests/test_guardrails.py` |
| No `ctx.app` — features reach the window shell only through the frozen `ViewerContext` accessors (§5.9) | `tests/test_ctx_app_burndown.py` (`CTX_APP_BUDGET = 0`) |
| No `ctx._x` scratch attributes, and no `ctx`-taking function called with the raw `app` / `self` — including the module-qualified `sc.foo(app)` spelling. Call sites are scanned in `review/` **and** `tests/`, since a test handing a real-app fixture to a `ctx` function is the same defect (§5.9) | `tests/test_frozen_ctx_guardrail.py` |
| The `ViewerContext` window-service accessor set is closed — after the A5 teardown it is exactly `{"window"}`; every other window service is now a held collaborator (`ctx.notify` / `ctx.figures` / `ctx.coordinator` / `ctx.persistence` / `ctx.features`), and adding a new accessor is a reviewed act (§5.9) | `tests/test_ctx_service_accessors.py` |
| `AppRuntime` is live-object-only — `persistence/` never imports `app_runtime` (§5.9) | `tests/test_app_runtime.py` |
| `process_microscopy` / `image_table` controller line budgets | `tests/test_monolith_budgets.py` |
| No function crosses cyclomatic complexity 40 unless it is on the allowlist, and the allowlisted functions' **total** cannot grow — the per-function check alone let an existing debt function grow without limit, and the total's not-slack twin banks every decomposition's saving so it cannot be spent later | `tests/test_complexity_ratchet.py` (`TOTAL_ALLOWLISTED_CC_BUDGET`), with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| `services.remote_runner`'s import surface is its `__all__`: no file reaches any other name through it, by any of four access forms under any spelling of the import (relative and `importlib.import_module` included), and it re-exports nothing outside it (§6.4) | `tests/test_remote_runner_facade.py`, scan in `tests/_facade_scan.py`, bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| Every control the Properties panel binds to a pref key is in the measured roster for its figure, is bound once, shows the stored value when the panel is rebuilt, and writes its own key and no other when moved; the hand-wired Error bars control reaches `PlotState` | `tests/test_properties_control_contract.py` |
| `process_microscopy` re-exports nothing; callers import a `pipeline.*` name from its owner, and tests patch the orchestrator's own binding only at a listed seam, never reading a seam name through it (§6.2) | `tests/test_process_microscopy_facade.py`, scan in `tests/_facade_scan.py` |
| No test patches a name on a module that only re-exports it — the patch rebinds an alias nothing reads and the test measures nothing. A re-export application code looks up at call time (through a module alias, or a function-local `from … import`) is a live target and is not flagged | `tests/test_no_patch_misses_its_target.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| A Python subclass of a Qt class is declared at module scope, never inside a function: declared inside a builder with methods closing over `ctx`, the Home notes box kept every closed `ReviewApp` alive (§10.4) | `tests/test_qt_subclasses_live_at_module_scope.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| A closed `ReviewApp` is collected, leaves no top-level widget, PySide wrapper or app-class object behind, and a window closed mid-drain runs no deferred builder after it is gone (§10.4) — slow lane, run by hand | `tests/test_a_closed_review_app_is_freed.py` |
| A closed minimal shell with the Playground built is collected and leaves no top-level widget behind (§10.4) — fast lane | `tests/test_a_closed_shell_is_freed.py` |
| A menu or toolbar action whose signal is connected is built with `widgets.owned_action`, never by `addAction(text)` (§7) — fast lane | `tests/test_connected_actions_are_owned.py`, bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| `core/plot_style`, `barplot/{controller,collect}` and `export/{style,sidebar_view}` serve only names they define, apart from declared re-exports that are live and are the owner's own object (only `plot_style.follows_theme`); each name in `services.remote_runner.__all__` is the object its owner defines (§5.8, *Plotting import paths*) | `tests/test_plotting_facades_are_frozen.py`, bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| Every literal `lazy` / `lazy_names` / registry `_import_attr` target names something its module defines | `tests/test_lazy_targets_resolve.py`, bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| Split View is one-line removable — uninstalled, the resolvers collapse to single-tab (§5.10) | `tests/test_split_view.py::test_not_installed_is_single_tab` |
| Build profiles: a subset boots + loads, the strip plan matches the runtime filter, and the binary drops the excluded features' deps (§5.3 *Build profiles*) | `tests/test_feature_profile.py`, `tests/test_derive_profile.py`, `tests/test_profile_build.py` |
| CSV / batch export produces the expected values, and the single-plot and batch paths agree byte-for-byte | `tests/test_csv_batch_export_eval.py` (drives a real headless `ReviewApp`) |
| Never hardcode a colour or a pixel size (§3, §8) — allowlisted for colormap/palette data and the `__main__` demo blocks; `datasets/` is out of scope while its tool pages consolidate | `tests/test_hardcoded_tokens.py` |
| Every divider frame carries a name the QSS styles, so it paints a 1 px `border_subtle` hairline rather than Qt's 3 px etched default (§8) | `tests/test_divider_naming.py` |
| A well token is judged by `util.well_token`, never a local whole-token regex (§15) | `tests/test_well_token_single_parser.py` |
| A removable feature's state slice is reached from outside that feature through `state.feature_slice(name)`, never by attribute. `AppState.__getattr__` **raises** for a slice whose feature is not in `FEATURES`, so a profile build without it fails at the access — and `getattr(ctx.state.stats, "pairwise", [])` does not help, because the default covers a missing *attribute* on an object that already exists and reaching the object is what raises. Removability is read from `profiles/full.toml`, so a slice whose feature is kept forever (`bar`, `preview`, `review_image`) is not the subject; `features/registry.py` is exempt because every access there sits inside that feature's own activation hook, and the guard fails if that exemption stops describing a real access | `tests/test_disabled_feature_slices.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| `swallow` and `swallowed` are not swapped. They are near-identical names with opposite call shapes — a context manager and a call for inside an `except` block — and swapping them fails only when the line runs. `with swallowed():` raises **before** the body, so the work it was meant to guard never happens; `swallowed()` outside a handler logs a suppression with no exception in flight, which reads as a failure that did not occur | `tests/test_safe_helpers_used_right.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| A text-mode subprocess names its codec. `text=True` alone decodes the pipe with `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)` — UTF-8 here, the ANSI codepage on a user's Windows box — so a stream that reads correctly for the developer mojibakes the remote's `✓` / `→` markers for them and raises `UnicodeDecodeError` out of a reader thread on the first byte the codepage has no character for, skipping the `proc.wait()` behind it | `tests/test_subprocess_text_decoding.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| A context menu is opened through `widgets/menu_exec.exec_menu`, never `QMenu.exec` directly. `QMenu.exec` blocks in Qt's C++ event loop with nothing offscreen to close it, and unlike a dialog's `exec` it **cannot** be monkeypatched — Shiboken exposes it as a static/instance overload, so an entry in `_MODAL_CALLS` would write a class attribute that instance lookup ignores and measure nothing. The seam is ordinary Python, so the autouse fixture patches that instead; the guard also rejects `from widgets.menu_exec import exec_menu`, which binds the name past the patch's reach, and sees a raw `.exec()` on any name bound to a `*Menu(...)` construction, not only one called something with "menu" in it. A menu built in the function that opens it goes through `exec_transient_menu`, which deletes it afterwards: parented to a long-lived widget, a per-opening menu otherwise lives as long as that widget, and five openings of a job-queue row's menu left ten alive (`tests/test_transient_menus_are_disposed.py`) | `tests/test_menu_exec_seam.py`, with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| No `logging.Handler.emit` creates or arms a Qt timer — `emit` runs on the thread that logged the record, so a timer built there never fires and its teardown raises `killTimer` from another thread. Handlers marshal through `core.worker_bridge.GuiLogRelay` (§10.1) | `tests/test_log_handler_marshalling.py` (static) + `tests/test_log_handler_thread_safety.py` (behavioural), with bite cases in `tests/test_guards_bite.py` |
| `pipeline/`, `util/`, `services/` and `domain/` import no Qt and no `widgets` at any nesting; `data/` too, but for one allowlisted module (§5, §13) | `tests/test_qt_free_layers.py` |
| …and reach none *transitively* either: a Qt-free module may not import, at module scope, a module that imports Qt. Reading each file's own import list misses a one-hop detour through `core/`, which is how `domain/stats_compute` came to raise `ImportError: libQt6Core.so.6` while every docstring cited the direct check as its guarantee. The fix for such a hop is a function-local import, which is why only module-scope edges are followed (§5) | `tests/test_qt_free_layers.py::test_a_qt_free_layer_stays_importable_without_qt` |
| A `feature_slice("…")` names a slice some feature registers, and `_FEATURE_STATE_OWNERS` covers exactly the registered set. A misspelled name answers `None` in *every* build, so the branch it guards is dead everywhere — silently (§5) | `tests/test_feature_slice_names.py` |
| No Datasets tool imports another Datasets tool, so each stays independently deletable (§6b) | `tests/test_datasets_tool_isolation.py` |
| Every Datasets dashboard ends a run through the shared outcome setters rather than its own copies (§6b) | `tests/test_datasets_dashboard_outcomes.py` |
| Every Datasets tool controller owns its worker through `DatasetToolController`, and the one tool whose worker cannot be interrupted still reaches its own stop method (§6b) | `tests/test_datasets_controller_lifecycle.py` |
| The plot-card roster is written once **and completely** — the shell reads `plot_card_actions.PLOT_CARD_ATTRS` rather than restating the names, and every `PlotCard` a feature registers is in it (§5.3) | `tests/test_plot_card_roster.py` |
| The Response figure follows the Screen/Publication toggle through the shell's own loop, and its free text artists are drawn in the theme's ink | `tests/test_response_follows_the_plot_theme.py` |
| A free `ax.text` / `ax.annotate` / `ax.plot` on a themed figure is coloured from `tokens_for` **and** tagged `follows_theme` — neither an ink colour without the tag nor no colour at all (§5.3) | `tests/test_theme_ink_artists_are_tagged.py` |
| The Analyze layout readout renders `plan_input_layout`'s message rather than composing its own sentence about the folder, so the preview and the run cannot disagree (§6.1) | `tests/test_layout_readout_single_source.py` |
| Every per-cell render-mode lookup in the Image Table names the channel it is for, so a cell never resolves its raw/corrected setting or its LUT window against a neighbouring channel's (§5.5) | `tests/test_image_table_channel_identity.py::test_every_render_mode_lookup_names_the_channel_it_is_for` |
| A Batch Export job closure reads no live control — the channel, value column, metric and scatter axes are snapshotted before the job loop, which pumps the event loop between jobs (§9.5) | `tests/test_batch_export_run_snapshot.py::test_no_per_job_closure_reads_a_live_combo`, `::test_a_scatter_job_reads_no_live_axis_control`, `::test_the_snapshot_is_taken_before_the_job_loop` |
| Every plot path reaches its ON cutoff through `on_cutoff_for_column` rather than a raw per-channel accessor, so a spot tally is never measured against a fluorescence threshold (§5.6). An allowlist keyed on `(file, dotted enclosing function)` — the accessors stay reachable for the resolver and the Cell Gating rows, and the dotted chain stops a closure inheriting an exemption granted to a same-named closure elsewhere in the module — paired with two liveness tests: one fails on an entry naming no real reach, the other on a guarded name no module defines | `tests/test_on_cutoff_sweep.py` |

What is **not** statically enforced (and so relies on review + behavioural
tests): "never block the UI thread", route redraws through the `ReviewApp`
shim, lazy-tab-build `hasattr` guards, app-wide-selection discipline, the
bar-math / fold-change invariants, and the Playground↔pipeline parity (which has
its own dedicated parity test).

---

## 17. Troubleshooting (build, environment, runtime)

Moved here from the user manual (`README_WellViewer.md`): a *running* app is
already past install and build, so these recipes belong with the developer docs
rather than the in-app help drawer.

### Packaging / launch (macOS)

**`AllWell.app is damaged and can't be opened.`** — macOS quarantine on an
unsigned bundle. Fix:
```sh
xattr -cr /Applications/AllWell.app
codesign --force --deep --sign - /Applications/AllWell.app
```

**The app opens and immediately closes.** — Run the bundle from a terminal to
see the actual error:
```sh
dist/AllWell-<version>.app/Contents/MacOS/AllWell 2>&1 | head -100
```

**`No module named 'pkg_resources'`.** — `setuptools` was upgraded past v70 in
the mamba environment. Recreate the environment from scratch. Don't
`pip install setuptools` and don't `mamba update --all`.

### Environment (Windows)

**`Cannot uninstall Shiboken6 6.x.y, RECORD file not found` during
`pip install`.** — A conda-installed `shiboken6` (or `pyside6`) is sitting in
the env, and pip cannot uninstall it to satisfy the `PySide6==6.7.3` pin (conda
packages have no `RECORD` manifest pip can read). Two common sources:

1. An older `mamba create` line listed `pyside6` explicitly.
2. The conda-forge `matplotlib` meta-package pulled `pyside6` in as a
   transitive dep. **This is the gotcha.** The fix is to use `matplotlib-base`
   instead — same matplotlib, no Qt binding.

Bulletproof recovery (one block, paste into Miniforge Prompt at repo root):

```powershell
mamba deactivate
mamba env remove -n allwell -y
mamba create -n allwell python=3.10.14 setuptools=69.5.1 "numpy>=1.24,<1.25" scipy scikit-image matplotlib-base pillow imageio h5py vs2015_runtime -c conda-forge -y
mamba activate allwell
pip install --no-build-isolation -r requirements.txt
```

Do NOT include `pyside6` or `matplotlib` in the mamba step — both pull
shiboken6 in via conda where pip can't remove it. PySide6 is installed by pip
from the requirements file; `vs2015_runtime` from conda supplies the MSVC DLLs
PySide6 needs.

**`VCRUNTIME140_1.dll` was not found / PySide6 import crashes.** — The
conda-forge MSVC redistributable isn't visible to PySide6. Verify
`vs2015_runtime` is in the env (`mamba list vs2015_runtime`) and re-activate the
env so the conda `DLLs` directory is on PATH:
```powershell
mamba deactivate
mamba activate allwell
python -c "from PySide6 import QtWidgets; print('OK')"
```

**`pip install` fails on tensorflow with "no matching distribution".** —
TensorFlow 2.13.0 ships Windows wheels for Python 3.10 and 3.11 only. Confirm
with `python --version`. If you're on 3.12+, recreate the env pinning
`python=3.10.14`.

**`scripts\build_executable.ps1` reports "PyInstaller is not importable".** —
The active env doesn't have the deps installed. Activate the env first and
re-run pip:
```powershell
mamba activate allwell
pip install --no-build-isolation -r requirements.txt
```

### GPU / models / build output

**`No GPU device found` / TensorFlow not using Metal.** — Install
`tensorflow-metal`:
```sh
pip install tensorflow-metal==1.1.0
python -c "import tensorflow as tf; print(tf.config.list_physical_devices('GPU'))"
```

**StarDist model download fails (SSL error).** — Pre-download the model on an
unrestricted machine and copy `~/.keras/models/` across.

**`No module named 'stardist'` in the built app.** — The build forgot the
PyInstaller hooks. Make sure `_Docs/_Installation/hooks/` (notably
`hook-stardist.py`) was on the spec path.

**The built bundle is > 900 MB.** — Normal. TensorFlow + Numba + LLVMLite +
SciPy + Matplotlib account for the bulk.

### Runtime / data

**Segmentation / smFISH / Image Table show "No images found".** — Check that
your results directory contains `<well>_out.zip` files. The viewer reads
top-hat-filtered fluorescence (`*_tophat.tif`), masks (`*_labels.tif`), overlays
(`*_overlay.png`), and smFISH-processed channels (`*_smfish.tif`) from inside
those ZIPs. If channel tokens differ from what the viewer expected, re-open the
directory — `pipeline_info.json` is re-read on every open.

**A large Image Table grid gets slower rather than failing.** — Decoded frames
live only in the bounded decode cache, sized from installed RAM. A grid whose
pixels exceed that budget re-decodes evicted frames on each pass, so a plate-wide
walk of large frames takes longer to Generate; it no longer grows resident memory
with the grid, which is what previously turned a big grid into failed allocations
and cells that would not load. If a grid is slow, narrow the well / timepoint
selection or crop the view.

**A well has fewer fields of view than were imaged.** — Its FOV-groups failed
during processing; the well still wrote a complete-looking CSV from the ones that
succeeded. `ls <output_dir>/errors/` names every failed (well, field, timepoint)
with its exception type, and `cat` on one gives the traceback. The most common
cause is the scratch volume filling mid-run (§6.2) — the message reports the free
space at the moment of failure. Recover with `--incremental`, which reprocesses
only the (fov, timepoint) groups missing from each CSV and merges them in; the
rows already present are correct, so nothing needs deleting.

**A well's error bars are missing and its bars carry `n/a`.** — Nothing was
computable for that spread. Either the well has one replicate (one field with
FOV errors on; one above-threshold cell without), or its FOV labels don't
identify its fields — check the status line and log at load, which name any well
in the second state. `n/a` is deliberately distinct from a bar with no marker at
all: the marker means "not computed", its absence with error bars on means the
spread is genuinely tiny.

**A whole well's per-field numbers are blank.** — Its `fov` column carries no
usable labels, so the fields pooled into one. The cause is upstream: the image
filenames don't split into as many tokens as `--filename_schema` has fields, so
the pipeline wrote an empty FOV for every row (it now warns once per filename
shape during the run). The well's mean and fraction are still valid — they don't
depend on the field labels — but anything per field is undefined until the CSVs
are rewritten with a schema that matches the filenames.

**An Image Table cell reads `(no mask)`.** — That cell's ≥threshold or mask view
has no segmentation mask for its (well, timepoint, FOV). The Image Table renders
nothing rather than showing the intensity image in its place, so a threshold view
is never half silhouettes and half pictures. Check that the well's output carries
a `*_labels.tif` for that frame, and that its FOV / timepoint tokens match the
fluorescence filenames — the mask and the image resolve through the same matcher,
so a mask that is missing here is genuinely absent or named differently.

**Cells that read `(no image)` come back on the next Generate — when the source
was the problem.** — An empty scan that might be about the moment is not cached
across passes: one that raised, one whose walk was cut short (`ScanResult.partial`),
or one whose dataset folders were not there (an external drive spinning down, a
share that dropped). Those only cost the pass they happened in, so press Generate
again rather than reloading. An empty scan that is an answer about the dataset —
the folders exist and the walk finished (`frame_load._scan_is_definitive`) — *is*
kept until the dataset is reloaded, and the log says so ("not searched again until
the dataset is reloaded"). Re-asking it on every pass re-walked every well's
archives on every zoom, LUT or crop change; on a plate brought back from a remote
run, whose raw inputs are not local, that was a full re-scan per change for every
Raw cell. A directory still being written that should now hold the frames needs a
reload. The log records each empty scan and each discovery failure with the well
and channel.

**Wells fail with `OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor`.** — One of the
volumes the run touches is a network mount. macOS's SMB client invalidates every
open file handle when the session drops and reconnects, and a run's parallel I/O
is more than enough to provoke that; whatever had files open at that moment
fails. `mount | grep <path>` confirms the protocol — `smbfs` gives `EBADF`, NFS
would give `ESTALE`. The first question is *which side* the errno came from, and
the log now says so rather than leaving it to be guessed:

- **A local run.** Check the `Scratch  :` line at the top of the run log — it
  must **not** be a network path (it defaults to `~/.allwell/scratch`; set
  Analyze → *Scratch disk* or `--scratch_dir` to a local SSD if it isn't). That
  line carries the bulk of the run's I/O. What remains on the output dir is the
  two per-well result writes, which retry through the transient; if they still
  exhaust the budget the message names the volume. Lower `--workers` to cut the
  concurrent load, or write results locally and copy to the NAS afterwards.
- **A remote / Slurm run.** The pipeline runs on the cluster, so a well that
  fails there is the *cluster's* storage; the failure is logged by the pipeline
  itself, on the remote's stdout, with the well label. Anything prefixed
  `[remote]` is the **client**, on this machine, and points at the input or
  output volume instead — staging reads the whole plate off the input volume and
  every fetched well is published onto the output volume. Both retry, and a
  `[retry]` line in the run log is the early warning that a volume is flapping
  before it costs a well. See §6.5 for the full list of crossings.

**A remote run fails while staging, before anything uploads.** — Same cause as
above, on the input volume: staging copies every `<WELL>.zip` off it back to
back. The copy retries, and the exhausted-budget message names the mount. Copy
the plate to local storage and point All-Well at that copy.

**A remote run dies immediately with `EnvironmentLocationNotFound: not a conda
environment`.** — The pipeline's conda env isn't usable where the run looked for
it. The run log names the env it chose (`[remote] conda env: name allwell` or
`prefix <path>`), and the guard prints the host, conda's base, and every env
conda can see. Three causes, and the guard says which:

- *A directory exists at the prefix but is not an environment* (no
  `conda-meta/history`) — an env creation that died part-way, usually a full
  home-directory quota. The guard names the directory and prints the `rm -rf`
  line; remove it yourself (check the quota first, or the next install stops the
  same way) and then re-run Analyze → Remotes → *Bootstrap*. All-Well does not
  delete it for you. Bootstrap stops with the same note rather than attempting
  the `conda create` that conda would refuse. See §6.6.
- *The host was never bootstrapped*, or its env was removed. Run Analyze →
  Remotes → *Bootstrap* for that host.
- *The host's `remote_python` points at an env that isn't there.* The field is
  only consulted when the user has changed it from the placeholder; either fix
  the path or clear it to fall back to the env named `allwell`.

A value that isn't shaped like `<env>/bin/python` cannot name an environment;
the runner keeps the name selector and says so on a `[remote] warn:` line
rather than guessing at a prefix.

**Bootstrap fails with `CondaValueError: prefix already exists`.** — The same
half-created directory, on a build that predates the check above. Remove the
prefix the message names and re-run Bootstrap.

**Auto-threshold reports `timepoint unknown`.** — `pipeline_info.json` doesn't
have a schema that names a `tp` or `timepoint` field. Re-run the pipeline with
the correct `--filename_schema` so the JSON sidecar carries the right field map.

**Bar-plot timepoint dropdown is empty.** — Either no wells are selected, or the
CSVs don't have a `timepoint_hours` column. Confirm the schema you ran the
pipeline with included a `timepoint` field. Single-timepoint experiments show
one entry (e.g. `0`).

**The grouping step produces no zip files.** — Schema or separator does not
match the filenames. Make sure `well` points at the right token, the separator
is right, and the token is a valid plate position (`A01`–`H12` or `A1`–`H12`).
The schema used is logged at the start of every run.

**Channel dropdown shows a different channel than the plot.** — Should be fixed;
if you ever see it again it means the active channel state and the combo got out
of sync. Refresh the dataset (Open the same folder again). File a bug.

---

## Change history

This document is a map for **making changes**, not a changelog — it describes how
the app is structured today, not how it got here. Do not add `(vX.Y.Z)` markers,
"new in", "was changed to", or any other note of *when* something landed: prose
here states what is true now. The only version claims that belong in this file
are the current-release ones (the header and the `version.py` directory-map
entry), which `tests/test_doc_version_sync.py` pins.

For the history of a given file or feature, use `git log` / `git blame` and the
PRs on GitHub; deep design rationale for specific subsystems lives in the topic
docs under `_Docs/Markdowns/` (see §13). When you change the architecture, update
the relevant section above rather than appending a version note here.
